In the binary odd-squarefree case the known least-prime valuation supplies the wrong-branch baseline \(p_1+1\). Independent exact-integer checks verified 53 odd-local prefix cases and the complete binary recursion on 20 odd squarefree indices below 160.

originality.rationale: The same-day broader published archive record gives a normalized residual theorem and, for squarefree indices, contains the signed residual identity as a special case when the Möbius sign is known. Crucially, that record explicitly does not resolve the binary squarefree sign ambiguity. The audited result adds the sign-free two-branch valuation comparison and a complete exact binary recursion for odd squarefree indices. Shunia's primary abstract advertises the least binary prime and successive Archimedean logarithmic peeling, not this higher local sign-free recursion. Thus the core signed identity is covered, but the final sign-free squarefree extraction theorem is not mechanically implied by the inspected prior statements.
residual_risks: Both cyclotomic extractor records are dated 2026-09-18 without finer public ordering, and Shunia's full text was inaccessible through the attempted routes. A contemporaneous local formulation could therefore overlap more strongly than the material actually read shows.

limitations: The index and base are assumed known; this is not an efficient integer-factorization algorithm.
